messages:
maria: quick heads-up — after PTQ (int4) bringup of compact-ranker-v2 we're seeing MRR jitter on the short-query slice (len<=6). ndcg pretty stable but mrr drops intermittently across runs :thinking:
aj: oh interesting, which dataset/slice and seed? any candidate-ordering change?
sam: can you paste the eval diffs? small deltas sometimes are noise from sampling or non-deterministic sorting.
maria: put a quick diff below from three sequential runs (same holdout, same seed) — note the third run has a big mrr dip:
```
run A: ndcg@10=0.842 mrr@10=0.613
run B: ndcg@10=0.840 mrr@10=0.609
run C: ndcg@10=0.839 mrr@10=0.576  <-- large drop
slice: short_queries len<=6 (3k queries)
model: compact-ranker-v2 int4 ptq
config: priming=enabled, kvprefix=on, batch=32
```
eva: priming + kvprefix + int4 seems like a perfect storm. we've seen priming change topk ordering for short queries before. can you try with priming disabled? also confirm that candidate pool ordering is stable (hash sort vs original order).
maria: running two quick checks: 1) disable priming 2) disable kvprefix. kicking off now with same seed 42. cmd: `./eval/run.sh --split holdout --slice short_queries --seed 42 --priming false`
perf-bot: started eval job 1799997778 on runner-12 (eta ~12m) :rocket:
aj: also check whether PTQ introduced any small floating-point tie-breaking changes; int4 often changes logits enough to flip near-ties. try running deterministic scorer with `PYTHONHASHSEED=0` and sort_by_text fallback.
sam: if result persists, let's run paired A/B: A=FP16 baseline, B=int4 PTQ with same preproc and no priming and compare paired differences per-query. that will tell if it's quant noise or priming ordering.
maria: results back (quick):
```
no-priming: ndcg@10=0.839 mrr@10=0.611
no-kvprefix: ndcg@10=0.841 mrr@10=0.608
priming+kvprefix: ndcg@10=0.839 mrr@10=0.576
```
maria: so disabling priming almost completely restores MRR. kvprefix alone not the culprit. priming + int4 leads to unstable reordering on short queries.
eva: aha. sounds like priming is shifting logits in the low-margin regime and quantization amplifies the tie flips. approach: 1) add short-query priming guard (skip priming if len<=6) 2) add deterministic tie-breaker (stable sort on doc_id) 3) add a regression check in the bringup playbook that runs the short-query slice with priming on/off.
aj: agree. add a unit in the eval harness that records per-query tie-score deltas and flags >X flips. We should also log raw logits for the top 5 candidates for short queries for a sample of 100 queries.
sam: quick patch idea: in ranking postprocess, when top-k scores within eps (e.g., 1e-4), break ties by doc_id to avoid non-deterministic ordering. low-cost and likely to stabilize MRR.
maria: i'll open a tiny PR with: - priming guard for short queries - stable tiebreaker - extended short-slice smoke in bringup CI. will run PTQ again after.
perf-bot: deployed candidate-sort-stable v1.1 to staging (rollout 10%) :thumbsup:
maria: thanks — will update thread after PTQ rerun. initial hypothesis: not a dataset selection issue but an interaction between priming and quantized low-margin score flips.
eva: if this is confirmed, we should also update the model catalog note for compact-ranker-v2 int4: "avoid priming for short queries or enable stable-tie policy".
aj: one more note — add this check to the NDCG/MRR alerting: if mrr delta > 0.02 on short slice after quant deploy, page oncall.
maria: agreed. will file a follow-up ticket and link to this thread. cheers.
